t.d: Painting of wooden buildings with linseed oil and earth pigments, first on trim, by the early 1900s on whole facades.
t.tech: Thin coats of boiled linseed oil paint brushed onto timber
t.mat: Boiled linseed oil, earth and mineral pigments
ctr: Swedish National Heritage Board (Kulturkulör colour tool, discontinued)
t.auth: Solvent-free oil-and-pigment recipe; historic colour schemes

t.d: Waterproof polished lime plaster of Moroccan hammams, palace and riad bathrooms and qadad roofs.
t.tech: Single thick coat compressed and polished with hard stones, sealed with olive-oil soap
t.mat: Lime plaster, marble or limestone sand, black or olive-oil soap, pigment
t.auth: Lime rather than Portland cement; stone-polished surface; periodic soap resealing

t.d: Inlaid-clay floor tiles of medieval England, mass-produced again in the Gothic Revival.
t.tech: two-shot moulding of coloured clay inlay backfilled with body clay, then fired
t.auth: pattern runs through the body (inlay 3–6.4 mm), not painted on the surface

t.d: Hand-cut glazed tile mosaic in Islamic geometric patterns.
t.tech: glazed squares cut by hand with an adze-hammer, assembled face down and backed with plaster
t.mat: Fez grey kaolinitic clay, metal-oxide glazes
t.auth: Fez pieces cut after firing and fit tightly; Tétouan pieces cut before firing, looser fit

t.d: Dutch tin-glazed earthenware, including some eight hundred million tiles over two centuries.
t.tech: underglaze cobalt painting on white-glazed earthenware
t.mat: blend of local, Tournai and Rhineland clays; tin glaze; cobalt oxide

t.d: Iberian painted tin-glazed tilework for façades, churches and interiors.
t.tech: alicatado, cuerda seca, cuenca/arista, maiolica painting, later transfer-printing
ctr: Real Fábrica de Louça do Rato

t.r: Puebla and Tlaxcala, Mexico; Talavera de la Reina, Spain
t.d: Tin-glazed majolica tradition shared by Mexico and Spain, on UNESCO's list since 2019.
t.tech: two firings, hand painting in natural pigments that blur into a milky crazed glaze
t.mat: black Amozoc and white Tecali sands with natural clays; tin and lead glaze
t.auth: DO hologram, potter's signature, workshop logo, base inscription with artist's initials and Puebla

t.d: Quarrying and splitting of Welsh slate for roofs, floors and slabs.
t.tech: quarrying, splitting and dressing slate to standard sizes
t.auth: Penrhyn named sizes from Duchess (24 × 12 in) down to Single

t.d: Hand-moulding of brickearth bricks on a stock, fired with 'Spanish' ash and cinders.
t.tech: clay pressed into a mould on an iron-faced stock, struck off with a wire, dried and fired
t.auth: original soft lime mortar cleans off; new bricks painted to pass as second-hand are unfit for face work

t.d: Zen dry landscape of raked gravel and set stones representing water.
t.tech: raking gravel (samon) into line, wave, scroll and check patterns
t.auth: True Shirakawa-suna has jagged-and-smooth grains that hold raked lines for weeks; crushed quarried granite holds them poorly.

t.d: Kiln production of hard white charcoal from ubame oak, designated an intangible folk cultural property of Wakayama in 1974.
t.tech: Slow kiln pyrolysis (about 240 °C for 120 hours), final firing near 1,000 °C, then smothering in damp earth, sand and ash
t.auth: Yellow label of the Wakayama Prefectural Charcoal Cooperative; Regional Collective Trademark (2006); metallic ring when struck
